goal: Find an exact adaptive evidence policy that chooses the next action after each realized outcome, minimizing worst-case actions needed to isolate the active finite hypothesis.

planner_contract.hypothesis_update: After observing outcome y from action a, retain exactly hypotheses whose possible-outcome set for a contains y.
planner_contract.objective: minimize worst-case number of additional actions until one hypothesis remains
planner_contract.unresolved_terminal: If >1 hypotheses remain and no remaining action can guarantee eventual singleton resolution, return unresolved rather than forcing a decision.
planner_contract.tie_break: return all optimal first actions; canonical policy chooses lexicographically first optimal action.

hypotheses.claim: The recursive policy value equals exhaustive enumeration of all remaining action/outcome branches for the frozen finite fixture.
hypotheses.rule: Any depth or terminal-status mismatch refutes A1.

hypotheses.claim: The minimum worst-case identification depth is 2 actions, with exactly two optimal first actions: direct_detection_calibration and direct_target_state_assay.
hypotheses.rule: Any different depth or optimal-first-action set refutes A2.

hypotheses.claim: Choosing repeat_one_survey or repeat_four_surveys first has worst-case depth 3 because a zero-detection outcome preserves all three active hypotheses before the two direct channels are still needed.
hypotheses.rule: Any repeat-first worst-case depth other than 3 refutes A3.

hypotheses.claim: For known truth absent::p1, the canonical calibration-first policy observes p=1 and terminates after exactly one action.
hypotheses.rule: Any additional action requirement or wrong terminal hypothesis refutes A4.

hypotheses.claim: Removing either direct_detection_calibration or direct_target_state_assay makes exact worst-case singleton identification impossible with the remaining finite action library.
hypotheses.rule: Any finite worst-case resolving policy after removing either direct channel refutes A5.

boundary: Worst-case set-valued planning is guarantee-oriented and does not optimize expected information gain.
An adaptive branch may terminate earlier than the worst-case depth.
Finite action libraries may be insufficient; unresolved is a valid terminal result.
Idealized direct channels remain upper-bound evidence types.
